result.summary: Wrote `docs/validation/evidence/equipment-authority-lifetime-2026-09-20/semantic-fault-plan.json` defining exactly two executable, isolated fault units against `godot/scripts/core/inventory.gd` only, each as byte-exact `old`→`new` string replacements with `expected_occurrences: 1`, for Astra's deterministic clone campaign. Nothing was run, and no production or test file was touched by this response. Unit `equipment-authority-strong-ownership-restored` (fault 1) adds a tiny `StrongEquipmentReference` inner class next to the field declaration (`get_ref()` still returns the target only while `is_instance_valid(target)` holds, so Node-freed and never-set-target cases behave identically to today), retypes `_equipment_authority` from `WeakRef` to that class, and changes the single setter line `_equipment_authority = weakref(authority)` to `_equipment_authority = StrongEquipmentReference.new(authority)`. Every other gate (`has_equipment_authority()`, `_equipment_authority_refusal()`, `_attests()`) is untouched and keeps calling `.get_ref()` exactly as before, so this isolates the retention-cycle regression alone. I traced this against the actual accepted test bodies and expect it to fail `test_real_gear_inventory_residents_mutually_release_without_unbind` (the decisive real mutual-release witness — Inventory now strongly retains the real bound Gear, recreating the cycle ADR 0187 removed), plus `test_expired_refcounted_authority_refuses_all_four_gates_with_state_unchanged`, `test_audit_refuses_orphan_lot_after_authority_expires_without_normalization`, `test_explicit_unbind_refuses_with_live_equipped_lots_even_after_authority_expires`, and `test_a_strong_per_call_local_survives_the_authority_dropping_its_sole_external_owner`, since none of their stub authorities can actually expire anymore once the field itself holds them strongly. Unit `equipment-authority-expired-wrapper-admitted` (fault 2) changes only the `_equipment_authority.get_ref() == null` branch inside `_equipment_authority_refusal()` to return `REFUSE_NONE` instead of `REFUSE_INVALID_EQUIPMENT_AUTHORITY`, leaving the never-bound `REFUSE_NO_EQUIPMENT_AUTHORITY` branch and `_attests()` itself untouched. Tracing the real gate order, this makes `preflight_detach_to_equipment()` and `preflight_attach_equipped_lot()` wrongly report success for an expired authority (preflight never calls `_attests()`), and makes `attach_equipped_lot()` on an already-equipped lot wrongly succeed and mutate state (since `_attests()` returning false no longer blocks it once the presence gate is bypassed), while `detach_lot_to_equipment()` still refuses but under the wrong code (`REFUSE_NOT_AN_EQUIPPED_RECORD` instead of the expected `REFUSE_INVALID_EQUIPMENT_AUTHORITY`). I expect this to fail `test_expired_refcounted_authority_refuses_all_four_gates_with_state_unchanged` and `test_expired_node_authority_refuses_all_four_gates_after_explicit_free` (both assert exact error codes, `assert_false(op.ok)`, and byte-identical `state_bytes()` on all four gates — the attach case in particular now actually writes state) and `test_explicit_unbind_refuses_with_live_equipped_lots_even_after_authority_expires` (its final `preflight_detach_to_equipment` check now wrongly succeeds). `test_audit_refuses_orphan_lot_after_authority_expires_without_normalization` is deliberately excluded from unit 2's expected failures, since `_audit_lot_placement()` calls `_attests()` directly and never goes through the mutated gate function. Both units target only `godot/scripts/core/inventory.gd`, add well under 50 total new lines, and leave every other refusal path, the transaction/journal machinery, and the 14 currently-passing tests' other assertions structurally reachable so a clone still compiles and runs the full suite without parse or GDScript errors — only the listed assertions are expected to genuinely fail.
